The implementation latches only on `local-changes-dropped` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:181) and `onWriteFailure`; `sync-state.ts:44` names `PersistDisabled` in a comment but nothing subscribes to it. A grep across packages/frontend/src for `PersistDisabled|persist-disabled` returns only that comment. Grep PersistDisabled in **/*.d.ts (no node_modules present to confirm SDK surface)

verdict.reason: The design doc specifies `durable` as a three-fact conjunction including "no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off" (offline-local-persistence.md:416-418) and a chip row "Document too large / too slow to snapshot -> durable false" (:428, risk row :511). The implementation computes `durable: !lost && !writesFailing` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:128), where `lost` latches only from `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...)` (:181) and `writesFailing` only from the store's `onWriteFailure` (:122); durable-document-context.ts:26-29 documents the same two-fact model. I searched repo-wide (all packages and docs, not just frontend/src) for `[Pp]ersist[-_]?[Dd]isabled|persistDisabled` — the only hits are a restating comment in sync-status/sync-state.ts:44 and the design doc — and enumerated every string-keyed `doc.subscribe('...')` call in packages/frontend/src (only `local-changes-dropped`, `sync`, `presence`, `others`). wafflebase-doc-store.ts carries no size/frame-budget latch of its own, and an SDK-side persistence latch would simply stop calling the store, so it cannot be inferred indirectly. The originating task plan (20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:129-134) confirms the latch was designed to fire on LocalChangesDropped only, and its one deferred chip item (3.4) concerns tooltip wording, not this conjunct — so the omission is not a recorded deferral. Consequence: an acceptance criterion from the design ("the chip tells the truth about durability in every case") is unmet, and the chip can promise local durability for a document the SDK stopped persisting — the one direction the design says must never fail. The version gate (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24, MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 vs pin 0.7.22) makes it currently dark but the doc calls the bump "the whole switch". I could not inspect the SDK's event surface (no node_modules), but that is uncertainty about implementability, not about implementation — no counterexample exists in this repository.

finding.summary: The whole feature is unreachable on the pinned SDK: `@yorkie-js/react` is 0.7.22 while `MinClientKeyVersion` is 0.7.23, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and both opt-in entry points are hidden
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/package.json pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`; yorkie-capabilities.ts sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx), the chip offer, and `useDurableDocument`'s eligibility. As shipped, no user can opt in, so the design's primary Goal — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it" — is unreachable on this build. The design anticipates the gate ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed"), but the Rollout section describes PR 4 as a dark launch "bounded by who turned it on", which presumes somebody can.

verdict.reason: Every element of the presence claim checks out in the tree. packages/frontend/package.json:66 pins "@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"; packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:414-418 injects that literal pin string as __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__; packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24 sets MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23" and supportsClientKey() (:76-82) compares them via atLeast (:44-57), so it is statically false on this build with no runtime override. All three opt-in/eligibility surfaces are behind that gate: the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx:35), the chip's offer (components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:146), and the durable client mount (components/collab-document-provider.tsx:196). The repo's own task doc concedes the state (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:242-246, and the unchecked manual-smoke item at :220-221). Consequently the design's primary Goal (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:46-49) — edits surviving a reload on a device where the user asked for it — is unreachable as shipped, while the Rollout section (:482-484) describes PR 4 as a dark launch "bounded by who turned it on", which presumes someone can turn it on. I considered refuting on the grounds that the gate is deliberate and documented (:193-197) and that the upstream prerequisite (yorkie-js-sdk#1357) may not be released, but without the originating issue's acceptance text I cannot establish that shipping the user-facing outcome entirely dark was sanctioned, so no named refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, is not guarded away, and an unmet user-facing outcome is squarely in the spec-conformance lane.

finding.summary: `durable` omits two of the three terms the design specifies, so the chip can over-promise durability
finding.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees states: "`durable` is the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, and the store is not failing its writes", and the table below it maps "IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing)", "Quota exhausted after eviction" and "Store writes failing" to `durable = false`. The implementation computes `durable: !lost` where `lost` is latched only by `DurableLossWatch` on the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event; nothing observes `WafflebaseDocStore` write failures, the quota-refusal path (`withQuotaRetry` rethrows and `evictOldest` returning false surfaces nowhere), or `PersistDisabled`. `useDurableDocument` gates on `supportsClientKey`, the preference, the scope and the Web Lock, but never on IndexedDB being usable. Consequence: in private browsing or on a full origin the durable client still mounts, the chip renders `Saved to this device` and the `beforeunload`/navigation guards are suppressed, while nothing is on disk — the exact direction the design ("the default is to under-promise") and the code's own comment in `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx` ("Over-reporting durability is the one direction this feature must not fail in") forbid.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual premise is wrong. `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:128` computes `durable: !lost && !writesFailing`, not `!lost`; `writesFailing` is latched (`:112`) by an `onWriteFailure` callback handed to the store at `:122`, and the surrounding comment (`:94-111`) names this explicitly as the "store is not failing its writes" term of the design's three-fact conjunction. The store honours it: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1193-1220` reports a write failure on every arm of `withQuotaRetry` — non-quota errors at `:1205` (whose comment names "a database that will not open (private browsing)"), `evictOldest` returning false at `:1210` (the design's "Quota exhausted after eviction" row), and a failed retry at `:1216` — via `reportWriteFailure` (`:1226-1232`). Every write path (`saveSnapshot :539`, `appendChange :580`, `saveMeta :626`) opens the DB inside `withQuotaRetry`, so an IndexedDB that never opens lands there too. The signal reaches the chip: `use-sync-status.ts:75,220` feeds `useDocumentDurability()` into `deriveSyncState`, which demotes `saved-locally` to `not-saved` (`sync-state.ts:85`). Tests at `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:60-82` assert precisely the behaviour the finding says is missing, including that the latch never lifts. The finding's further claim that `useDurableDocument` should gate on IndexedDB being usable inverts the design, which states durability "is reported from whether the store actually works, never inferred" (`offline-local-persistence.md:136-138`). Only the `PersistDisabled` term is unwired, but that is an SDK-emitted event assigned to PR 1 (`:476`) covering the oversized-document row — not the private-browsing/full-origin over-promise the finding claims as its blocking consequence, which is demonstrably handled.
